PACKET: {"id": "F1", "task": "Change personal notification preferences without changing the team's defaults.", "evidence_type": "Authored synthetic packet; no executed browser observation.", "facts": ["The account menu opens 'My notifications'. Its Apply button changes only the current member's preferences, confirmed by a supplied synthetic before/after trace.", "A separate owner-only screen is titled 'Team defaults'. Its Apply button changes defaults for newly added members; existing member preferences stay unchanged.", "Both screen headings and explanations are visible next to their controls. The tested account is owner.", "The stakeholder proposes one shared Apply button to remove duplicate terminology. There is no evidence of a wrong-scope action or inaccessible labels."]}
REPORT A: Limited review of authored synthetic evidence; no live interaction or human observation. The supplied trace supports successful personal changes without affecting team defaults. Visible headings and explanations distinguish both Apply controls; no scope defect is supported. Preserve personal-only updates, owner-only team administration, new-member default scope, and existing members' preferences. The proposed shared Apply button addresses no evidenced obstacle and could obscure those distinctions; retain the working separation unless new evidence establishes a problem. Proposed acceptance check: change My notifications and verify only that member changes; adjacently change Team defaults and verify new-member defaults change while existing preferences remain unchanged. With authorized role fixtures, verify a non-owner cannot change team defaults. These checks are proposed, not executed; the owner packet does not independently verify non-owner enforcement or human discoverability.
REPORT B: Limited review of authored synthetic evidence: personal-preference changes affect only the current member; team defaults affect new members and preserve existing preferences. Visible headings and explanations support the intended scope distinction. No interface defect or wrong-scope action is supported. Retain the separate controls; the proposed shared Apply button has no evidenced benefit and could weaken scope separation unless equivalent context is preserved. This is a recommendation about the proposal, not a verified regression. Proposed acceptance check: change personal preferences and verify team defaults and other members remain unchanged; then change team defaults and verify only a newly added member inherits them. Any cross-scope mutation fails. Live persistence, non-owner permissions, accessibility and human interpretation remain unverified. For human follow-up, ask someone to change only their own notifications and explain which settings they expect to change.

PACKET: {"id": "F3", "task": "Publish a revised schedule to subscribers while leaving a private draft unannounced.", "evidence_type": "Authored synthetic packet; no executed browser observation.", "facts": ["A private draft has Save draft and Publish buttons. Save draft updates private content and sends no notification in the supplied synthetic trace.", "Publish displays the audience count and a checkbox 'Send subscribers an update', checked by default. The dialog also includes Cancel.", "The stated requirement allows publishing with or without notification. The trace with the box unchecked publishes the schedule without sending an update; Cancel preserves the draft.", "No irreversible action was executed outside the synthetic trace. REPORT A: Limited authored synthetic evidence supports private saving, publication without notification, and cancellation preserving the draft. No current contract violation is shown. Preserve private Save draft, the separate publication decision, audience visibility, notification choice, and Cancel recovery. The checked default is disclosed; this packet does not establish informed human consent or demonstrate notification delivery when checked. A single Save action addresses no evidenced obstacle and risks conflating private persistence, publication and subscriber updates. Retain distinct actions unless a replacement demonstrably preserves those decisions; shorter labeling alone is no benefit. Proposed acceptance check: Save draft must retain private changes without publication or notification. Adjacently, Publish with the checkbox unchecked must publish without updates, while Cancel preserves the private draft without publishing; an authorized synthetic checked-path test should verify the stated audience and update behavior. Any silent publication, unwanted update or lost cancellation path contradicts the proposed simplification's adequacy. No live irreversible action or human observation occurred.
REPORT B: Limited review of authored synthetic evidence: Save draft preserves private work without notification; Publish provides audience information, optional notification and Cancel. The unchecked path publishes without an update, satisfying the stated optional-notification requirement; Cancel preserves the draft. No supported defect warrants replacing these controls with a single Save action. Retain the explicit distinction between private saving and publication, plus notification choice and cancellation. A single label has no evidenced benefit and would need to preserve these distinct outcomes. The checked notification path and real delivery remain unverified; the default alone does not establish an error. Proposed acceptance check: Save draft changes private content only; Publish unchecked changes public content without an update; Publish checked sends the intended update to the displayed audience; Cancel changes neither publication nor draft content. Any unintended publication, update or draft loss fails. No live interface or human-participant evidence was assessed.
